solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Ruined health on diet eating duck dish (4-2-3-4)

indicatorNotes.Ruined: ruined letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
indicatorNotes.eating: the anagram swallows the duck, holding it inside

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

annotation.surface: Someone whose health has been wrecked by a diet that includes a duck dish.
annotation.walkthrough: The rearranged twelve letters take in O, so all thirteen are mixed together. Toad-in-the-hole is a British dish of sausages baked in batter.
annotation.definitionFit: Toad-in-the-hole is a traditional British dish of sausages cooked in Yorkshire pudding batter.

entries.clue: Branch manager Greene tours abroad (4,7)

indicatorNotes.abroad: abroad can mean scattered widely, so the letters are spread out and rearranged

annotation.surface: A bank's branch manager called Greene travelling on overseas tours.
annotation.walkthrough: "Branch manager" reads as a bank job, and Greene looks like a novelist's name; the branches are on trees.
annotation.definitionFit: A tree surgeon looks after trees, cutting and managing their branches.

entries.clue: Pervasive quality of first-class travellers (5)

blocks.note: A is the top grade, as in A1
the Roma are a travelling people

annotation.surface: A remark about the all-pervading atmosphere among people travelling first class.
annotation.walkthrough: "First-class travellers" looks like one phrase about train passengers; it splits into A and ROMA.
annotation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive quality that pervades something, as in an aroma of scandal.

entries.clue: What you do in pub close to crapulent bankrupt (9)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: what you, the solver, do to this clue

annotation.surface: What a drunken regular gets up to in the pub before going broke.
annotation.walkthrough: IN(SOLVE)N then T. "What you do" addresses the solver directly: you SOLVE. Crapulent means drunk or hungover.
annotation.definitionFit: Insolvent means unable to pay one's debts, which is what bankrupt means.

entries.clue: You shouldn’t have clipped sea monkey (7)

indicatorNotes.clipped: a clipped word has had its end cut off

blocks.note: said on receiving a gift; ta is British slang for thanks
MARINE, meaning of the sea, with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: A polite protest on being handed a strange gift: a sea monkey.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sea monkey" looks like one creature, but sea belongs to the wordplay. TA is British slang for thank you.
annotation.definitionFit: A tamarin is a small South American monkey.

entries.clue: Tory no more whose time has passed (2-3)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes a person (one whose time has passed) rather than naming one
annotation.surface: A former Conservative whose political moment is over.
annotation.walkthrough: The words appear as CON then EX in the clue, but the answer puts EX first. "Time" is prison time: an ex-con has served it.
annotation.definitionFit: An ex-con is a former convict, someone whose prison time is behind them.

entries.clue: Frau converted, absorbed in additional prayer (3,6)

indicatorNotes.converted: converted letters are changed into a new arrangement
indicatorNotes.absorbed in: the rearranged letters are taken inside another word

blocks.note: other = additional, as in other reasons

annotation.surface: A German woman who has converted to a new faith and is absorbed in extra prayer.
annotation.walkthrough: O(URFA)THER. Frau, the German for a married woman, is only letters here; "converted" suits the religious surface.
annotation.definitionFit: The Our Father is the Lord's Prayer, named from its opening words.

entries.clue: Measure pain after leaving hospital (3)

indicatorNotes.after leaving: what remains once H has left the word

blocks.note: H = hospital, as on road signs; it is removed

annotation.surface: Assessing how much pain a patient is in when discharged from hospital.
annotation.walkthrough: "Measure pain" reads as a nurse's task, but Measure is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An ell is an old measure of length, used for cloth.

entries.clue: Backed augury one found in movie? (4)

annotation.surface: A backed prophecy and someone turning up in a film.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful nod to the film title Finding Nemo: he is the one found in that movie.
annotation.definitionFit: Nemo is the clownfish who is found in the animated film Finding Nemo.

entries.clue: Cécile is dancing with Mr D? (10)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancing letters move about into a new order

annotation.surface: A Frenchwoman called Cécile dancing with a mysterious partner, Mr D.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mr D" reads as a man's name, but D stands alone as the definition: the capital letter is shaped like a half circle. The question mark flags the definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A capital D is a straight line closed by a semicircular curve, so D can suggest a semicircle.

entries.clue: One attacking a crew member reported (8)

indicatorNotes.reported: what is reported is heard, so the answer sounds like the phrase

blocks.note: a sailor is a member of a ship's crew

annotation.surface: A news report that one of a ship's crew has been attacked.
annotation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech "a sailor" and assailer sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain agent noun: to assail is to attack, and the -er ending makes the person doing it.

entries.clue: Tight times just around the corner (6)

blocks.note: times as in multiplication: two by three

annotation.surface: Hard financial times are coming soon.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tight times" reads as austerity; tight means mean with money, which NEAR also means in British usage.
annotation.definitionFit: Something nearby is close at hand, just around the corner.

entries.clue: Dear Welsh leopard destroyed residence (8,3)

indicatorNotes.destroyed: destroyed letters are broken up and put back in a new order

blocks.note: bach is a Welsh term of endearment, like dear

annotation.surface: A Welsh home wrecked by a leopard.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dear Welsh" reads like a letter opening; bach is the Welsh endearment, used much like dear or love.
annotation.definitionFit: A bachelor pad is a flat or house where a single man lives, a residence.

entries.clue: High-street trader avoiding alcohol daily (3-7)

blocks.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaner who comes each day

annotation.surface: A shopkeeper on the high street who has gone teetotal every day.
annotation.walkthrough: "Daily" looks like an adverb; in British English a daily is a domestic cleaner.
annotation.definitionFit: A dry-cleaner runs a shop, usually on the high street, cleaning clothes.

entries.clue: Firms criticise one blocking move towards south (9)

indicatorNotes.blocking: the pieces block the way by sitting inside another word

annotation.surface: Businesses criticising someone who is blocking a relocation to the south.
annotation.walkthrough: "Move towards south" looks like a relocation, but it is two separate pieces, with the criticism and the one lodged inside the first.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the commercial sense, the plural matching the plural definition.

entries.clue: Agent to slow insect devouring pitch (9)

indicatorNotes.devouring: the insect eats the pitch, taking it inside

annotation.surface: A pesticide wanted to slow down an insect that is chewing up the pitch.
annotation.walkthrough: RE(TAR)DANT. The insect must be the specific RED ANT, not just ANT.
annotation.definitionFit: A retardant is a substance, an agent, that slows a process such as burning.

entries.clue: Rhine wine or pop? (4)

blocks.note: the British name for German white wine from the Rhine, from the town of Hochheim
to pop is British slang for to pawn, as in pop your watch

annotation.surface: A choice of drinks: German wine or a fizzy soft drink.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pop" poses as fizzy drink beside the wine, but it is the verb to pawn.
annotation.definitionFit: Hock is German Rhine wine; to hock something is to pawn it, to pop it.

entries.clue: Goethe for one discarding an original thought (4)

indicatorNotes.discarding: to discard is to throw away, as with a card from a hand, so AN is thrown out of the word

blocks.note: Goethe is an example of a German

annotation.surface: The poet Goethe abandoning an early idea.
annotation.walkthrough: "Original" here means first, starting: the germ of an idea is its seed.
annotation.definitionFit: A germ is the seed or starting point of an idea, an original thought.

entries.clue: Sons leaving to track bird and rabbit directly (4,6)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the sons walk out of the word, so the S that stands for them goes

blocks.note: STALK = track, with S for sons removed

annotation.surface: Hunters leave to stalk a game bird and a rabbit.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rabbit" is British slang for chatter or talk, so rabbit directly means speak frankly; the hunting surface hides it.
annotation.definitionFit: To talk turkey is to speak plainly and frankly about a matter.

entries.clue: Beat with undesirable acceleration in dance (7)

blocks.note: a is the symbol for acceleration in physics

annotation.surface: A dancer finding the beat but speeding up in an unwelcome way.
annotation.walkthrough: "Beat" and "acceleration" feel musical, but they are LAM and the physics symbol A.
annotation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian partner dance.

entries.clue: Really popular female performance (2,4)

annotation.surface: Praise for a woman's performance that was very well received.
annotation.walkthrough: "Really" looks like an intensifier for popular; it is the definition standing alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are sentence adverbs used to insist on the truth, as in 'really, it was' and 'in fact, it was'.

entries.clue: Motorist finally learned to put foot down (5)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the word's end, its last letter, is used

blocks.note: to read a subject is to learn it, as in reading law

annotation.surface: A driver at last learns to press the accelerator.
annotation.walkthrough: "Put foot down" suggests accelerating in a car; here it is simply stepping.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for stepping, as in treading on a toe; the motoring sense of the phrase is the surface's decoy.

entries.clue: Old woman hot in desert run (8)

indicatorNotes.in: hot is placed in desert, read literally: one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: ma = mother, an old woman in slang

annotation.surface: An elderly woman sweltering as she runs through a desert.
annotation.walkthrough: MA then RAT(H)ON. "Desert" wants to be sand; it is the verb, to rat on someone.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the marathon is the classic long-distance road race of 26.2 miles.

entries.clue: Host hasn’t run very small outfit (5)

indicatorNotes.hasn’t: the word does not have R, so R is removed

blocks.note: a host is a large crowd, a throng
R = run, as in cricket scores; it is removed

annotation.surface: A party host who hasn't run up anything bigger than a tiny outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: "Host" suggests a person throwing a party; here it is a multitude, as in a host of angels.
annotation.definitionFit: Playful understatement: a G-string barely counts as an outfit at all, hence very small.

entries.clue: Wants facts about English team heading for relegation (10)

indicatorNotes.about: the facts go around the other pieces
indicatorNotes.heading for: the head of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A demand for the facts on an English football team facing relegation.
annotation.walkthrough: D(E SIDE R)ATA. Relegation is the drop to a lower division in British football leagues.
annotation.definitionFit: Desiderata are things wanted or needed, wants.

entries.clue: Purpose Kennedy periodically reveals (3)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of kEnNeDy

annotation.surface: A Kennedy disclosing their aim from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: The even letters of Kennedy spell END.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of goal, as in 'the ends justify the means'.

entries.clue: Surgical procedure breaks bone: my mistake! (4)

indicatorNotes.breaks: the operation breaks into the bone, sitting inside it

blocks.note: os is the Latin for bone, used in anatomy

annotation.surface: A surgeon breaking a bone during an operation and apologising.
annotation.walkthrough: O(OP)S. The surface reads as a surgeon's confession, which is exactly when you would say the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Oops is what you say to admit a small blunder: my mistake!

entries.clue: Poor dealt with for fencing blue Aston Martin? (13)

indicatorNotes.for fencing: fencing encloses, so the outer word surrounds the others

blocks.note: to do something is to deal with it
the Vantage is a model of Aston Martin car

annotation.surface: Someone badly treated for putting a fence around a blue sports car.
annotation.walkthrough: DI(SAD VANTAGE)D. The question mark shows Aston Martin stands for one model of the car, the Vantage.
annotation.definitionFit: Disadvantaged means lacking resources or opportunities, poor.
